verses.1: First of all, then, I urge that requests, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for everyone,
verses.2: for kings and for all who are in positions of authority, so that we may lead a quiet and peaceful life in all godliness and reverence.
verses.3: This is good and acceptable in the sight of our Savior God,
verses.4: who wants all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
verses.5: For there is one God, and one mediator between God and humankind, the man Christ Jesus,
verses.6: who gave himself as a ransom for all, at the appointed times—
verses.7: for which I have been appointed a herald and an apostle— I am telling the truth, I am not lying— a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
verses.8: I desire, then, that men pray in every place, lifting up holy hands without anger or argument.
verses.9: Likewise, women are to dress in respectable clothing, with modesty and self-control, not with elaborate braiding or gold or pearls or costly attire,
verses.10: but with what is appropriate for women who profess godliness— through good works.
verses.11: Let a woman learn in quietness with full submission.
verses.12: I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man, but to remain in quietness.
verses.13: For Adam was formed first, then Eve;
verses.14: and Adam was not deceived, but the woman was deceived and became a transgressor.
verses.15: But she will be saved through childbearing, if they continue in faith and love and holiness, with self-control.

notes:
Notes
- v. 14: The phrase "ἐξαπατηθεῖσα ἐν παραβάσει γέγονεν" is translated to capture the sequence of events: "was deceived and became a transgressor."
- v. 15: "σωθήσεται διὰ τῆς τεκνογονίας" is rendered as "will be saved through childbearing," reflecting the literal meaning, though the exact interpretation of "childbearing" as a means of salvation is a matter of theological debate.
raw:
[1] First of all, then, I urge that requests, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for everyone,
[2] for kings and for all who are in positions of authority, so that we may lead a quiet and peaceful life in all godliness and reverence.
[3] This is good and acceptable in the sight of our Savior God,
[4] who wants all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
[5] For there is one God, and one mediator between God and humankind, the man Christ Jesus,
[6] who gave himself as a ransom for all, at the appointed times—
[7] for which I have been appointed a herald and an apostle— I am telling the truth, I am not lying— a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
[8] I desire, then, that men pray in every place, lifting up holy hands without anger or argument.
[9] Likewise, women are to dress in respectable clothing, with modesty and self-control, not with elaborate braiding or gold or pearls or costly attire,
[10] but with what is appropriate for women who profess godliness— through good works.
[11] Let a woman learn in quietness with full submission.
[12] I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man, but to remain in quietness.
[13] For Adam was formed first, then Eve;
[14] and Adam was not deceived, but the woman was deceived and became a transgressor.
[15] But she will be saved through childbearing, if they continue in faith and love and holiness, with self-control.
---
Notes
- v. 14: The phrase "ἐξαπατηθεῖσα ἐν παραβάσει γέγονεν" is translated to capture the sequence of events: "was deceived and became a transgressor."
- v. 15: "σωθήσεται διὰ τῆς τεκνογονίας" is rendered as "will be saved through childbearing," reflecting the literal meaning, though the exact interpretation of "childbearing" as a means of salvation is a matter of theological debate.
